In the [[mathematics|mathematical]] field of [[graph theory]], the '''Barnette–Bosák–Lederberg graph''' is a [[cubic graph|cubic]] (that is, 3-[[regular graph|regular]]) [[polyhedral graph]] with no [[Hamiltonian cycle]], the smallest such graph possible.<ref>{{citation
 | first1 = D. A.
 | last1 = Holton
 | first2 = B. D.
 | last2 = McKay
 | author2-link = Brendan McKay (mathematician)
 | title = The smallest non-Hamiltonian 3-connected cubic planar graphs have 38 vertices
 | journal = Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B
 | volume = 45
 | issue = 3
 | year = 1988
 | pages = 305–319
 | doi = 10.1016/0095-8956(88)90075-5
 | doi-access=free}}</ref> It was discovered in the mid-1960s by [[Joshua Lederberg]], David Barnette, and Juraj Bosák, after whom it is named. It has 38 vertices and 57 edges.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Lederberg | first = Joshua | authorlink = Joshua Lederberg
 | doi = 10.2307/2314879
 | journal = [[The American Mathematical Monthly]]
 | mr = 0211895
 | pages = 522–527
 | title = Hamilton circuits of convex trivalent polyhedra (up to 18 vertices)
 | volume = 74
 | year = 1967| issue = 5 | jstor = 2314879 }}</ref><ref>{{citation
 | last = Bosák | first = J.
 | contribution = Hamiltonian lines in cubic graphs
 | location = New York
 | mr = 0221970
 | pages = 35–46
 | publisher = Gordon and Breach
 | title = Theory of Graphs (Internat. Sympos., Rome, 1966)
 | year = 1967}}</ref><ref>{{MathWorld|urlname= Barnette-Bosak-LederbergGraph|title=Barnette-Bosák-Lederberg Graph|mode=cs2}}</ref>

Other larger non-Hamiltonian cubic polyhedral graphs include the 46-vertex [[Tutte graph]] and a 44-vertex graph found by [[Emanuels Grīnbergs]] using [[Grinberg's theorem]].
The Barnette–Bosák–Lederberg graph has a similar construction to the Tutte graph but is composed of two Tutte fragments, connected through a [[pentagonal prism]], instead of three connected through a [[tetrahedron]].
Without the constraint of having exactly three edges at every vertex, much smaller non-Hamiltonian polyhedral graphs are possible, including the [[Goldner–Harary graph]] and the [[Herschel graph]].
